title: Change Brief
description: The structured read of a change, authored once at Stage 1 and reused by every channel run. Audience IDs (A*), message IDs (M*) and milestone IDs (T*) are the spine of every run: Stage 2 maps content to them and Stage 4 proves none went unaddressed.

trading_name.description: What appears in the comms. Legal name rarely does.

title.description: The practitioner's own name for the change. Carried into the plan as engagement_title.

type.description: Drives channel and tone advice. 'hybrid' is the common real case — model it, don't force a false choice.

type_evidence.description: Why that call was made. Keeps a judgement call auditable.

what_is_changing.description: The one-sentence factual statement. Everything else elaborates it.

rationale.description: The why. Not optional — a comms without one reads as a decree, and it is the single most common omission.

rationale_confidence.description: An inferred rationale must never be written as though the sponsor said it.

what_is_not_changing.description: Named reassurance stops more rumour than any amount of positive messaging. Always ask for it.

whats_in_it_for_me.description: Required. A segment with no articulable WIIFM is a segment nobody has thought about yet.

effort.description: e.g. '10 minutes'. Stating it raises completion.

optional.description: true is the honest encoding of 'nothing to do'. An empty action string is not.

concerns.description: Anticipated objections. Drives which messages lead.

manager_cascade_required.description: High-impact segments usually need a manager brief before the mass comm.

text.description: The message in its intended voice, not a topic label.

priority.description: qa_comms hard-fails on an uncovered must-land; warns on a supporting.

audience_ids.description: Lets a single-audience run compute its own coverage denominator.

evidence.description: What backs the claim, where it makes one.

sensitivity.description: Gates the channel. market-sensitive may not be planned onto an open channel.

date_confidence.description: Not garnish. Publishing an indicative date as confirmed burns a programme's credibility faster than anything else, so Stage 4 requires indicative dates to be hedged in the draft text.

visible_to_audience.description: Internal programme gates must not leak into an all-staff comm.

why_this_messenger.description: The messenger is content, not metadata. The same words from a line manager and from a comms mailbox land differently.

approver.description: approved:false at draft time is normal. It is reported at handover, not failed.

detail.description: The actual address, number or link

help_route.description: Structured, not prose, so its presence can be asserted mechanically. Every required action needs a route for when it fails.

embargo.description: Nothing may be published before this date/time.

prohibited_terms.description: Checked mechanically in Stage 4 — e.g. 'restructure', 'efficiencies', a competitor name.

open_questions.description: What the practitioner could not answer. These become visible [GAP]s downstream rather than confident invention.
